entry.title: b12550: ggml : add backend scheduler tests (#27258)
entry.content:
• Adds initial scheduler stress tests

  • Adds new sleep op to simplify scheduler testing

  • Adds testcase addressing #23321

  • Adds experimental vulkan GGML_OP_SLEEP

  • Improves structure and naming of previous tests. Adds new tests,
    including one which detects the nkvo-bug correctly, and validates the
    proposed hotfix.

  • Cleanup: Removes CUDA specific comments and nvtx-markers

  • Fix: forgot to add sleep specific test case

  • Fix oversights identified by CI

  • Drops default prints so that it behaves like other ctests. Adds -v flag
    to toggle this behavior

  • Fix: Early exit in CPU-only settings (cause for graviton CI fails)

  • Improves stress_test_linked_list by removing overlap with
    test_chain_all_backends and test_pair_user_inputs. The latter ones test
    either activations or user inputs in isolation and just once, whereas
    the stress test tests all combinations multiple rounds

  • Exclude ACCEL devices from new tests due to incompatibility

  • Fixes vulkan test failure in llvmpipe

  • Adds asserts, improves comments and some checks

  • Fixes nitpicks in white-space and variable naming

  • Adds comments that certain vk drivers could time OP_SLEEP incorrectly

  • Drops limitiation to CPU/GPU in test-sleep

  • Aligns OP_SLEEP guards in cuda with vk guards (input shape and
    contiguity)

  • Implements feedback for OP_SLEEP to work in place (no copy)

  • Apply non-code suggestions from JohannesGaesslers code review

Co-authored-by: Johannes Gäßler johannesg@5d6.de

  • Removes struct backend_supports; enables tests to return skip, instead
    of only pass/fail

  • Make clang-tidy happy

  • Removes sched_backend_caps, improves create_test_scheduler according to
    feedback (L149)

  • Removes "name" field from struct sched_check in favor of
    ggml_set_name/ggml_get_name

  • Drops unnecessary shader_clock.comp test and guards

  • Replaces sched_ prefixes with helper_ prefix

  • Moves test suite to new RAII types for better memory management

  • Adds sleep option to test_chain_all_backends

  • Adds sleep option to first-run arm of the y-shaped test

  • Fix switchcase order for legibility in stress_test_dag

  • Simplfies stress_test_linked_list via double for-loop

  • Adds pseudo-random input to stress_test_linked_list, and runs all
    transitions both with and without CPU input (next to activation copy as
    input)

  • Fix RPC Proto patch due to GGML_OPS bump

  • Adds ggml-cpp.h treatment to test-sleep.cpp

  • Adds TODO pointers for subsequent additional tests.

  • Apply suggestion to ggml.h

Co-authored-by: Johannes Gäßler johannesg@5d6.de

  • Apply suggestion to tests/test-backend-sched.cpp

Co-authored-by: Johannes Gäßler johannesg@5d6.de

  • Apply suggestion to tests/test-backend-sched.cpp

Co-authored-by: Johannes Gäßler johannesg@5d6.de

  • Fixes node compatibility check to not take buffer locations into account.
    This led to skipped tests due to incorrectly rejected ops due to wrong buffer locations in multi-GPU (which is one of the scheduler behaviors under test)

  • Apply batched suggestions from gg code review

Co-authored-by: Georgi Gerganov ggerganov@gmail.com

  • Completes callsite change of gg-suggestion

  • Switch test-sleep from std::chrono::steady_clock::now() to ggml_time_us
    to avoid mac clock drift and spurious test failures.
    This makes the test a bit nonsensical on CPU (same clock checks itself),
    but the test still has merit on the other backends where
    independent device clocks are used.

Co-authored-by: Johannes Gäßler johannesg@5d6.de
Co-authored-by: Georgi Gerganov ggerganov@gmail.com

entry.title: b12549
entry.content:
llama: fixes for Inkling 2 attention mask (#32429)

  • llama : give Inkling2 its own relative-position attention input

The Inkling2 graph built its flash attention mask from the hybrid iswa
input and passed it to build_attn through a new kq_mask argument. That
argument let a caller pair its own dense mask with the kv_rows of
llm_graph_input_attn_kv_iswa, whose mask follows the per-sequence cell
lists whenever kv_rows is enabled.

Add llm_graph_input_attn_rel_pos instead. It owns dense KQ masks and the
query-to-cell distances, fills both from the same cells, and its
build_attn overload adds the per-head bias to its own mask and never
passes kv_rows. The iswa build_attn is back to its previous signature;
its body moves to build_attn_iswa_impl, which both overloads call.

Inkling2 now folds the per-query sink into the bias with and without
flash attention, so build_attn_mha no longer needs the per-query sink
path.

Assisted-By: Claude Opus 5.5 noreply@anthropic.com

  • inkling2 : make the expert weight scale and final logit softcap optional

Load both keys as optional and skip them when they are zero, as other
models do, instead of rejecting zero at load.

Assisted-By: Claude Opus 5.5 noreply@anthropic.com

  • llama : build kv_rows masks for the hybrid iswa memory

llm_graph_input_mem_hybrid_iswa checked its masks with
can_reuse_attn_mask, which expects kv_rows whenever they are enabled,
but built them dense. With a unified cache and flash attention the
check always failed, and hybrid iswa models (LFM2, LFM3, Inkling2)
never reused a graph. Build the masks with build_attn_inp_attn_mask,
like the plain iswa input.

Assisted-By: Claude Opus 5.5 noreply@anthropic.com

  • llama : make the relative-position input a hybrid iswa input

Address review: llm_graph_input_mem_hybrid_iswa_rel derives from
llm_graph_input_mem_hybrid_iswa and owns the attention and recurrent
inputs, so Inkling2 builds one memory input instead of two. Its
attention input is built with dense masks, can_reuse checks them as
dense, and its build_attn asserts that the mask has no kv_rows (TODO:
a kv_rows variant). build_attn_iswa_impl is now a static helper.

Assisted-By: Claude Opus 5.5 noreply@anthropic.com

  • llama : compose the hybrid iswa rel input, format inkling2

Address review: llm_graph_input_mem_hybrid_iswa_rel owns its attention
and recurrent inputs like the other composite inputs instead of deriving
from llm_graph_input_mem_hybrid_iswa.

Format src/models/inkling2.cpp like the other model sources: grouped
and aligned key and tensor loading, descriptive per-layer names, blank
lines and section comments between the steps, and cb() names for the
intermediate tensors. The graph is unchanged.

Assisted-By: Claude Opus 5.5 noreply@anthropic.com

entry.title: b12543
entry.content:
metal : CONV_2D tensor API for M5, split-K for all chips (#32542)

  • metal: add a tensor API conv_2d kernel and split long reductions

The conv_2d matmul kernel runs on simdgroup matrices only, and gives
each threadgroup the whole reduction of its output tile. On M5 this
leaves the tensor cores unused, and convolutions with few output
positions and a long reduction (IC * KW * KH in the thousands) run a
handful of threadgroups on an otherwise idle GPU.

Add kernel_conv_2d_mm_tensor for devices with the tensor API: like
kernel_mul_mm, it gathers the patches of 64 output positions into
threadgroup memory as the left operand and reads the kernel rows
from device memory as the right operand. Devices without the tensor
API keep the simdgroup kernel.

Both kernels can now split the reduction until there are enough
threadgroups: each split writes its partial sums to a buffer placed
after the output, as flash attention does, and a small kernel adds
them in a fixed order, so the result stays deterministic. CONV_2D is
marked as an op whose allocation may exceed its output size.

test-backend-ops -o CONV_2D passes, with and without
GGML_METAL_TENSOR_DISABLE.

CONV_2D, F16 kernel, us/run on an M5 Max:
[19,19,256,16] k [4,4,256,4096] 19008 -> 5235
[16,16,128,8] k [3,3,128,512] 333 -> 124
[1536,1536,32,1] k [3,3,32,64] 12086 -> 6512
[33,1,1280,1] k [3,1,1280,1280] s2 659 -> 33
[2054,1,768,1] k [7,1,768,768] 3161 -> 699

  • metal: walk the conv_2d patches incrementally, size splits by output

The patch gather of both conv_2d matmul kernels spent most of its
time on address math: 64-bit multiplies, divisions and four bound
checks per value. Walk the reduction index with 32-bit byte offsets
inside the image, updated by additions, with one unsigned compare per
bound; the host checks that an image fits. The tensor kernel no
longer gathers the reduction indices past the end of its split.

The number of splits now targets about 1M partial sums, with at least
3 reduction steps per split, instead of counting the tiles of one
kernel.

CONV_2D, F16 kernel, us/run on an M5 Max:
[19,19,256,16] k [4,4,256,4096] 4998 -> 4512
[1536,1536,32,1] k [3,3,32,64] 6721 -> 5354
[4096,1,1024,1] k [7,1,1024,1024] 2701 -> 2236
[2054,1,768,1] k [7,1,768,768] 1050 -> 871
with GGML_METAL_TENSOR_DISABLE:
[4096,1,1024,1] k [7,1,1024,1024] 9047 -> 8283

  • nit: share the CONV_2D simdgroup count between host and kernel

kernel_conv_2d_mm and its pipeline both hardcoded 4 simdgroups per
threadgroup. N_SG_CONV_2D in ggml-metal-impl.h now feeds the kernel
constant and res.nsg, so the dispatch and the kernel cannot drift apart.

  • metal: fall back to the generic conv_2d kernel for images past 4 GiB

The matmul conv_2d kernels walk the patches with 32-bit byte offsets
inside an image. Instead of asserting on nb13, compute the largest
offset actually read from ne/nb, which also covers strided views of
the input, and route images that do not fit to the generic kernel.

  • cont : comments
